title: AC-51 says the rules-loaded gate still blocks an edit after a rules change, but that gate only checks that rules-loaded.json exists
context: Issue 748 (Parts A-D) is built and committed (cdcf1f3d, 31add5c5, 25ff9e60, 445eb00f): the entry marker now goes stale only on docs/instructions/{stack,design-system,workflows}, so a change under docs/instructions/rules/ no longer re-blocks an agent. The issue and AC-51 assume the rule contract is still enforced separately: 'given rules-loaded.json recorded before a change under docs/instructions/rules/, when an edit is attempted after that change, then the rules-loaded gate still blocks it'. The code says otherwise: the pre-mutation rules-loaded capability (src/kernel/capability.ts, rulesLoadedCapability) returns no-op as soon as readRulesLoaded() finds the file; it never compares the record to the current rules. The completion gate (src/verification/repository rules-loaded gate) only goes INCONCLUSIVE when a newly applicable rule id is missing from the record (coverageGaps); an edited rule text it already covers passes. Before this change the entry gate's whole-docs/instructions staleness was what forced a re-read after a rule edit. So AC-51 cannot be proven without new code, and without it a mid-change rule edit is no longer re-forced before the next edit. Recorded data that makes a cheap check possible: rules-loaded.json stores rule_text_hash and the changed paths it was computed for, and computeRuleApplicability (src/context/rule-context.ts) can recompute the hash from the compiled store already read by the capability.

options.label: Make the pre-mutation rules-loaded gate also block when recomputing the applicable rule text hash for the recorded changed paths no longer matches rule_text_hash (the agent re-runs paqad-ai rules load); rule-script-map.yml and registry writes do not change rule text, so they do not re-block. AC-51 holds as written; adds one capability change, its test and a doc line

options.label: Keep the rules-loaded gate as it is and correct AC-51 through a spec change: an edited rule is not re-forced before the next edit; the completion gate goes inconclusive only when a newly applicable rule is uncovered, and the always-on rule scripts still enforce script-enforced rules

rationale: Owner chose the hash check: the pre-edit rules-loaded gate compares a hash of the loaded rule text and asks for a reload only when a loaded rule's text changed; map/registry writes never re-block; applicability growth stays a turn-end check.
